evals.prompt: Our SaaS home dashboard shows 12 same-size cards (MRR, ARR, churn, signups, DAU, MAU, NPS, tickets, uptime, CAC, LTV, ARPU). Nobody uses it. Redesign it.
evals.expected_output: Names the dashboard type (product home or strategic) and the one question it answers; applies the four-question KPI test and cuts to 3-5 headline KPIs with comparisons, targets, and definitions; pairs volume with quality; lays out KPI row, main trend, breakdowns/attention list, table with an ASCII wireframe; colors deltas by meaning (churn up is bad); moves the rest to reports; specifies per-widget states; global range in the URL.
expectations: Reduces headline KPIs to between 3 and 5
Each kept KPI has a comparison period or target
Layout puts the most important KPI first/top-left and follows KPI row, trend, breakdown order
Delta color is tied to whether the change is good or bad, not to arrow direction
Specifies loading, empty, and error states per widget
Removed metrics are moved to a report or secondary view rather than deleted without explanation

evals.prompt: Build a live operations dashboard for our payments team to watch during incidents. Data updates every few seconds.
evals.expected_output: Operational type: status line with text, SLO/threshold marked on charts, small multiples by region, recent errors table linking to traces; visible 'updated Xs ago', Pause, stale state; batches UI updates (10-30 s) and throttles when the tab is hidden; no layout shift; polite live-region announcements only for status changes; color paired with text.
expectations: Shows data freshness (e.g. 'updated Xs ago') and a stale state
Offers a way to pause live updates
Status is conveyed with text or icons in addition to color
Batches or throttles updates rather than re-rendering on every event
Thresholds or SLOs are shown against the metrics

evals.prompt: Set up the app shell for our Next.js B2B app: sidebar, header, user menu, and Cmd+K. It has Home, Inbox, Projects, Reports, Customers, Billing, and Settings.
evals.expected_output: Left sidebar (7 areas) ordered workspace switcher, search/palette, personal items, workspace sections, footer with settings and account menu; expanded ~240-280 px, icon rail with tooltips at tablet, drawer below 768 px; collapse state persisted without flash (cookie); header with breadcrumb, search, notifications; palette available everywhere with platform-correct hint (Ctrl+K on Windows), grouped results, shortcuts shown, accessible combobox; landmarks, skip link, aria-current; may reference shadcn Sidebar as a dated reference implementation.
expectations: Uses a left sidebar rather than top nav or a desktop hamburger
Defines responsive behavior including a drawer on small screens
Persists sidebar collapse state across reloads without a layout flash
Command palette shows Ctrl+K on non-Mac platforms and lists shortcuts on commands
Account menu places sign out last
Includes aria-current on the active nav item or a skip link to main content

evals.prompt: Our analytics dashboard takes 12 seconds to show anything because one API call computes all 9 charts. How should we restructure it?
evals.expected_output: One query per widget loaded in parallel with its own skeleton, error, and timeout; stream shell and KPI row first; pre-aggregate rollups; cache keyed by tenant, query, filters, and range with visible freshness; bound cardinality and downsample; server-side tenant scoping.
expectations: Splits the single call into per-widget queries loaded independently
Each widget gets its own loading and error state so one failure does not blank the page
Recommends pre-aggregation or caching with a visible freshness indicator
Cache keys or queries include the tenant so data cannot leak across accounts

evals.prompt: Build an orders table for our admin with sorting, pagination, and bulk refunds. About 80,000 orders.
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is a data table/admin CRUD task for data-dense-ui (server-side sort and pagination, alignment, bulk action safety), not a dashboard layout; a good answer does not add KPI rows, date-range comparison bars, or dashboard widget states.
expectations: Does not wrap the table in a KPI dashboard layout
Uses server-side sorting and pagination for 80,000 rows
Bulk refund shows the selection count and scope before acting
